METHOD: self_evolverec
COMPARISON MODEL FAMILY: gru4rec. Start from the supplied corrected baseline; keep its backbone family throughout search, including initial proposals, merging and debugging. Do not fall back to SASRec or another model family. Keep seed 42, maximum epochs 200, batches per epoch 200 and the supplied splits/evaluator fixed. All models use LEFT-padded histories: the readout must use the final nonpadding position, never count-1. BERT4Rec uses a reserved mask token with masked-target training and appended-mask inference; do not expose a shifted prediction target through bidirectional input. Preserve checkpoint and embedded predictor consistency. Diagnosis uses family-specific sample_batch and ModelView; keep log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items) compatible. One trained model/checkpoint per category; no independent score fusion.

MANDATORY SINGLE-MODEL EXPERIMENT: train one independent model per category.
Do not implement ensembles, bagging, boosting of independent predictors, stacking,
multi-seed/checkpoint averaging, score/rank voting, mixtures of independently fitted
experts, or neural scores combined with separately fitted transition/popularity scores.
Each category must load exactly one independently trained model/checkpoint at prediction.
Jointly trained internal layers/features of one network are allowed. Four category
models are necessary for routing and do not constitute an ensemble. All hypotheses,
code generation, debugging, reviews and memory use must respect this constraint even
if an upstream generic prompt suggests an ensemble. The host audits the actual
predictor before accepting validation scores; violations fail the trial and consume
their training budget. Do not read other trials or reuse their trained checkpoints.

the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),

train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.

Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

 ## Search results
Search results provide related ideas, but no verified exact match for a GRU with a jointly trained, randomly initialized title/description encoder. [Recformer (KDD 2023)](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/kdd23b.pdf) motivates learning recommendation-specific language representations rather than relying on coarse semantic features, combining language understanding and next-item objectives; its Transformer architecture is not a GRU replacement suitable here. [CLA-Rec (ICDM 2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884256/) aligns description embeddings with collaborative information, but requires pretrained language models. [ICMA (COLING 2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.222/) uses relevance-aware sequence augmentation and intent contrast, suggesting that positives should preserve behavioral intent rather than merely share vocabulary.

[DWSRec (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28786) directly identifies text-embedding anisotropy as a recommendation limitation; whitening improves its pretrained-text setting, while full whitening can damage useful semantic structure. A constraint-compatible hypothesis—not a demonstrated result from these papers—is a small title/description encoder trained from scratch, integrated with item-ID embeddings inside one GRU network. Keep next-item ranking primary; test weak target-conditioned contrastive supervision against an otherwise identical text-enabled model. Avoid treating textual similarity alone as evidence of the same next-item intent. Measure macro validation HR@10 alongside random-pair cosine similarity, covariance spectrum/effective rank, and positive-versus-negative score margins: stronger positive alignment alone does not establish better ranking or reduced anisotropy. Keep all components jointly trained within one checkpoint per category.

---

GRU4Rec’s established BPR-max loss addresses weak gradients from averaging many easy negatives: softmax weights over negative scores emphasize difficult candidates, with negative-score regularization. The official implementation also supports popularity-tempered sampling and logQ-corrected cross-entropy, making these direct comparisons within the existing GRU backbone. [Original paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf), [official implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec). A 2024 sequential-recommendation study compared random, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive sampling; results varied by dataset and item popularity, providing no universal argument for harder negatives. [Study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276).

False-negative handling and sampling correction solve different problems. UFNRec (SDM 2023) identifies potential false negatives, reverses their labels and controls noise through output-space EMA and consistency regularization; high model scores alone do not establish true relevance. [UFNRec](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/1.9781611977653.ch6). A RecSys 2025 paper refines logQ correction because the positive is always included, whereas negatives are sampled; correction must reflect the actual sampling scheme. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331). Practical hypothesis: hold positional weighting and architecture fixed, compare regularized BPR-max against sampled cross-entropy, then separately vary negative count and uniform/popularity mixture. Use training histories to exclude known positives; treat tempered hard-negative weighting as an experimental safeguard, not verified false-negative detection. Deterministic top-k mining cannot simply inherit the original proposal probabilities for importance correction. Keep one trained GRU model per category and select through the pinned macro validation HR@10; stronger training margins alone establish no validation gain.

The closest direct precedent is [MTAM, CIKM 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598): temporal gates modify recurrent state transitions and information filtering; its time-aware GRU captures short-term intent.
